newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold seen running out of steam on upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold seen running out of steam on upside.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold needs to surmount resistance around $325/26 an ounce to extend the current run higher, but many players expect failure and an eventual return to test recent lows.
Silver would be weighed down on any move higher by resistance at its 10-day moving average around $4.32, analysts said.
GOLD -
Prices needed to convincingly break through resistance at $325.80, the high of July 4, to extend Thursday's short-covering rally.

The market had jumped in New York as heavily short funds covered some positions, and in early action on Friday spot gold resumed its upward track as buying in Tokyo and short covering in Hong Kong sent prices up to a high bid of $325.70.
Elliott Wave analyst John Sowden said early on Friday that the latest move was a short-term peak.
"The bounce now counts as complete near our $325.00 area, so the next move should be a decline to a new low. Higher resistance is 326.60," he said.
Rudolf Wolff analyst Martin Squires agreed that last week's 12-year low of $313.60, basis spot gold, was likely to be tested eventually.

Referring to the Comex August contract, he said, "We remain in favour of further downside tests and look to initial support at $318, then $314.50 whilst continuing to target $310 on a confirmed break,"
At 0740 GMT spot gold was quoted at $323.50/324.00, unchanged from Thursday's New York close.
SILVER -
The market recovered along with gold after touching fresh lows on Thursday, ending in New York at $4.26 per ounce.
But a downtrend was still in force and was likely to weigh on the market.
A declining 10-day moving average would put the damper on any thrust higher. It was at $4.32 at Thursday's close, edging down to $4.30 early on Friday.
Above there, resistance would be seen at $4.40, the highs of July 8 and 10. Support was pegged at the recent lows of $4.17/$4.18.

"With the technical indicators continuing to drift sideways, there is nothing to suggest a change of tack, as we remain bearish, with initial tests of $4.20 expected," Squires said, referring to the Comex September contract.
But Elliott Wave International, also referring to Comex prices, said it was possible that silver has begun a corrective rally to the $4.42-$4.45 area.
At 0740 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.26/4.28, unchanged from Thursday's New York close.
PLATINUM -
The market was running out of momentum on the upside, with resistance at $410, the high of July 8 and 11, a barrier in the way of further upside progress.
On any thrust higher, next resistance would be seen around $420.
Support was pegged at $394.
At 0740 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $407.00/410.00, up $1.00 from Thursday's New York close.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
